key_insight: PhysisForcing improves robotic video world models by explicitly reinforcing physical consistency at both pixel and semantic levels, reducing motion and interaction implausibility.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable training recipe for making video generators more reliable as closed-loop simulators and policy-training assets in robotic manipulation.
method: Pixel-level trajectory alignment loss supervises DiT features with reference point trajectories.
Semantic-level relational alignment loss matches DiT features to inter-region relations from a frozen video understanding encoder.
Focuses supervision on physics-informative regions rather than uniformly across the whole frame.
evidence_signal: Across R-Bench, PAI-Bench, and EZS-Bench, the method improved strong baselines, including +22.3% on Wan2.2-I2V-A14B and +9.2% on Cosmos3-Nano over base models, and raised WorldArena closed-loop success from 16.0% to 24.0%.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable trajectory and relation supervision from auxiliary models, so performance may be sensitive to annotation quality, encoder bias, or contact-heavy scenes outside the training distribution.
paper_title: PhysisForcing: Physics Reinforced World Simulator for Robotic Manipulation
